citations.field: Adjacent 少 entry; PDF p. 76 and continuation p. 77, printed pp. 64–65
citations.text: The adjacent 少 entry says 小 and 少 were originally one graph and were used alike in oracle-bone texts, then differentiated; it describes 少’s final diagonal stroke as a distinguishing mark. The entry continues onto printed p. 65. Both source scans were inspected; the relevant 少 and 小 forms are legible. This is the book author’s graphic account, not proof of a historical sound relationship.

consulted_citations.source: 李學勤主編,《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692
consulted_citations.field: 小 headword; PDF p. 76, printed p. 64
consulted_citations.text: The entry calls 小 pictographic and interprets its marks as tiny dust or sand particles, an early graph of 沙. It says the graph was extended to mean ‘small,’ opposite 大, and cites oracle-bone and bronze uses, including 《粹》1004 小雨. It also describes extensions to low status, contempt and youth, and says the bronze form had become corrupted, prompting Shuowen’s 八-plus-丨 explanation. Both attached page images were inspected; the printed headword, cited forms 小, 沙, 大, 八, 丨 and 《粹》1004 are legible. This verifies the author’s account, not the disputed sand interpretation.
